User.title: User
User.description: Represents a user account in the SplitWisePro application.

id.description: Unique identifier for the User entity.

email.description: The user's email address, used for authentication and login.

profileImageUrl.description: URL to the user's profile picture, typically obtained from an OAuth provider.

createdAt.description: Timestamp when the user account was created.

updatedAt.description: Timestamp when the user account was last updated.

Group.title: Group
Group.description: Represents a collection of users who share expenses together.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Group entity.

name.description: The name of the group (e.g., 'Vacation Crew', 'Housemates').

description.description: An optional description of the group's purpose or context.

creatorId.description: Reference to the User who created this group. (Relationship: User 1:N Group)

createdAt.description: Timestamp when the group was created.

updatedAt.description: Timestamp when the group was last updated.

GroupMember.title: GroupMember
GroupMember.description: Represents a user's membership within a specific group, linking users to groups.

id.description: Unique identifier for the GroupMember entity.

groupId.description: Reference to the Group this membership belongs to. (Relationship: Group 1:N GroupMember)

userId.description: Reference to the User who is a member of this group. (Relationship: User 1:N GroupMember)

joinedAt.description: Timestamp when the user joined the group.

nickname.description: An optional nickname for the user specific to this group, if they prefer to be called something else within this context.

Expense.title: Expense
Expense.description: Represents a single shared expense recorded within a group.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Expense entity.

groupId.description: Reference to the Group to which this expense belongs. (Relationship: Group 1:N Expense)

description.description: A brief description of what the expense was for (e.g., 'Groceries', 'Internet Bill').

totalAmount.description: The total monetary amount of the expense.

paidById.description: Reference to the User who initially paid the full amount of this expense. (Relationship: User 1:N Expense)

expenseDate.description: The date and time when the expense occurred.

createdAt.description: Timestamp when the expense record was created.

updatedAt.description: Timestamp when the expense record was last updated.

ExpenseShare.title: ExpenseShare
ExpenseShare.description: Represents a specific user's share or responsibility for a portion of an expense.

id.description: Unique identifier for the ExpenseShare entity.

expenseId.description: Reference to the Expense this share is part of. (Relationship: Expense 1:N ExpenseShare)

userId.description: Reference to the User who is responsible for this share of the expense. (Relationship: User 1:N ExpenseShare)

shareAmount.description: The exact monetary amount this user is responsible for in this expense. The sum of all ExpenseShare amounts for an expense should equal the Expense's totalAmount.

createdAt.description: Timestamp when the expense share record was created.

updatedAt.description: Timestamp when the expense share record was last updated.

Settlement.title: Settlement
Settlement.description: Records a payment made between two members within a group to settle outstanding debts.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Settlement entity.

groupId.description: Reference to the Group where this settlement occurred. (Relationship: Group 1:N Settlement)

payerId.description: Reference to the User who made the payment. (Relationship: User 1:N Settlement - Payer)

receiverId.description: Reference to the User who received the payment. (Relationship: User 1:N Settlement - Receiver)

amount.description: The monetary amount of the settlement payment.

settlementDate.description: The date and time when the settlement payment was made.

description.description: An optional description or note about the settlement.

createdAt.description: Timestamp when the settlement record was created.

updatedAt.description: Timestamp when the settlement record was last updated.

definition.description: Stores individual user profiles. Access is restricted to the owner matching `request.auth.uid`. The document ID is the user's Firebase Authentication UID.

params.name: userId
params.description: The unique ID of the user, matching their Firebase Authentication UID.

definition.description: Represents a collaborative group for splitting expenses. Includes denormalized 'members' map (e.g., `members: {userId1: 'admin', userId2: 'member'}`) for authorization independence, allowing direct query of groups a user is part of and securing subcollections without `get()` calls. The `creatorId` field specifies the user who initially created the group.

params.name: groupId
params.description: The unique ID of the group.

definition.description: Represents a user's membership within a specific group. The document ID is the `userId` of the member. This document includes a denormalized 'groupMembers' map (copied from the parent Group) for authorization independence.

params.name: groupId
params.description: The unique ID of the parent group.

params.name: memberUserId
params.description: The unique ID of the user who is a member of this group, serving as the document ID.

definition.description: Records individual expenses within a group. Includes denormalized 'groupId' and 'groupMembers' map (copied from the parent Group) for authorization independence and QAPs, ensuring only group members can access expenses.

params.name: groupId
params.description: The unique ID of the parent group.

params.name: expenseId
params.description: The unique ID of the expense.

definition.description: Defines a specific user's share of an expense. The document ID is the `userId` responsible for the share. Includes denormalized 'groupId', 'expenseId', and 'groupMembers' map (copied from the parent Group) for authorization independence.

params.name: groupId
params.description: The unique ID of the grandparent group.

params.name: expenseId
params.description: The unique ID of the parent expense.

params.name: userId
params.description: The unique ID of the user whose share this is, serving as the document ID.

definition.description: Records payments made between group members to settle debts. Includes denormalized 'groupId' and 'groupMembers' map (copied from the parent Group) for authorization independence and QAPs, ensuring only group members can access settlements.

params.name: groupId
params.description: The unique ID of the parent group.

params.name: settlementId
params.description: The unique ID of the settlement record.

firestore.reasoning:
The recommended Firestore structure prioritizes Authorization Independence and QAPs (Queryable Authorization Patterns) through extensive denormalization and structural segregation. 

1.  **Authorization Independence (No `get()` in rules):** To strictly adhere to the mandate of avoiding `get()` calls in security rules, the authorization context (i.e., who is a member of a group) is denormalized across all relevant documents. Each `Group` document will contain a `members` map (`{userId: role_string}`). Critically, every document within a group's subcollections (`GroupMember`, `Expense`, `ExpenseShare`, `Settlement`) will also contain a denormalized copy of this `groupMembers` map (or a simplified version indicating current user's membership status for simpler checks). This allows any security rule to evaluate access based solely on the `request.auth.uid` and the `resource.data` of the document being accessed, without needing to `get()` the parent `Group` document. This dramatically simplifies rule writing and debugging.

2.  **QAPs (Secure `list` operations):**
    *   **User-owned data (`/users/{userId}`):** A user can easily list their own profile by querying `users` where `userId` matches `request.auth.uid` (implicitly handled by path). This is a trivial QAP.
    *   **Collaborative data (`/groups/{groupId}`):** To enable efficient listing of groups a user is a member of, the `Group` documents contain a `members` map. This allows client-side queries like `db.collection('groups').where('members.request.auth.uid', '==', 'member')` (or `true` if roles are simplified) to securely retrieve only the groups the authenticated user belongs to. This directly supports the QAP requirement for collaborative data without relying on complex and inefficient rule logic or `get()` calls.
    *   **Nested data (`/groups/{groupId}/expenses`, `/groups/{groupId}/members`, etc.):** Since all subcollection documents (`Expense`, `GroupMember`, `Settlement`, `ExpenseShare`) also contain the denormalized `groupMembers` map, security rules can verify membership directly on the `resource.data` of the document. This ensures that any `list` operation on these subcollections (e.g., listing all expenses for a group) implicitly filters results to only those accessible by the requesting user via a secure rule, assuming the client provides the `{groupId}`. The critical part is that the `groupMembers` map on *each document* ensures the rule can validate membership without a cross-document `get()` for authorization.

3.  **Structural Segregation:** Data with different security postures is kept in separate collections. For instance, user profiles are distinct from collaborative groups. Within groups, members, expenses, shares, and settlements are logically nested and secured consistently by group membership.

4.  **Access Modeling:**
    *   **Private Data:** `/users/{userId}` ensures strict ownership.
    *   **Collaborative Data:** `/groups/{groupId}` with the embedded `members` map is the primary model for collaborative authorization. All nested data (`/groups/{groupId}/expenses/{expenseId}`, etc.) inherits and denormalizes this membership context.

This design mandates atomic writes when group membership changes, as all denormalized `groupMembers` maps must be updated across all affected documents. While increasing write complexity, this drastically simplifies read-time security rules and improves debugging, ensuring a secure and scalable Firestore backend for SplitWisePro.
